messages:
Alice M: Heads up — prepping guidance for customers who want strict tenant isolation on private installs. Two quick questions: 1) does the on-prem installer still rely on flat L2 segments by default or do we recommend VLANs per-tenant? 2) any RBAC caveats if ops need keystore access for SRE playbooks?
Bryan K: We default to a single L2 segment for smaller installs but recommend segmentation for production. VLANs per-tenant is our current prescriptive pattern.
Carla S: +1 VLANs. Also consider using L3 segmentation with route filters if customers are worried about L2 spoofing.
Raj P: Regarding keystore access — we require a short-lived service role for SRE runbooks. Ops shouldn't have persistent decrypt perms. Use ephemeral certs + KMS grant that expires.
Sophie L: For audits: make sure every KMS decrypt is logged with request metadata (principal, host IP, caller cert fingerprint). Customers keep that in Syslog/SIEM.
Alice M: Can we surface the recommended netpol / eBPF guard in the private docs? Customers ask for simple drop-in configs.
Carla S: I'll paste a minimal netpol snippet we give for tenant-ingress isolation:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-cross-tenant
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          tenant-id: "${TENANT}"
```
Carla S: That's minimal; we also recommend eBPF L3/L4 clamps on the host for spoof protection.
Bryan K: Note: VLANs + netpol isn't a full-proof tenant fence — you also need to lock host-level bridges and block promiscuous mode. Add a host daemon policy to disable `ip link set promisc on`.
Raj P: Re: RBAC changes — if we add an "SRE-KMS-Checkout" role, what audit hooks do we want? I propose KMS decrypt events annotated with `runbook_id` and `triggered_by` tags so we can tie to incidents.
Sophie L: +1. Also push the KMS request ID back into our internal audit-log pipeline so correlation is trivial (SIEM crosswalk).
Alice M: For incident response: if a tenant claims data exfil, do we want a standardized lockdown play? e.g., revoke grants, push deny ACLs, shift traffic to canary overlay?
Bryan K: Lockdown checklist we use internally: 1) revoke all active KMS grants for affected tenant principals, 2) quarantine node(s) via cloud provider security groups / VLAN ACLs, 3) rotate ephemeral certs, 4) enable packet capture for 72h retention (forensically).
Carla S: One warning: revoking KMS grants is asynchronous and can take seconds-minutes. Have a fallback read-only mode for customer app so they don't blow up critical processes.
Raj P: On the KMS integration — customers running in air-gapped installs: we support an HSM appliance or bring-your-own KMS proxy. For BYOK proxies, we require mTLS with client certs pinned to an admin CA.
Sophie L: Audit logging differences to call out in docs: hosted vs. private. Hosted: we provide token-level logs to customer portal. Private: they must ship their audit-forwarder; recommend stamping logs with `redwood.node` and `tenant-id`.
Alice M: Any quick checks we can add to the installer to assert isolation is correct post-install?
Bryan K: Yes — run a 5-check smoke test: VLAN tag visibility, ARP probe across segments blocked, netpol egress blocked to other tenant CIDRs, KMS decrypt attempt with an unrelated tenant principal fails, audit-forwarder reachable.
Carla S: We can implement that as `rwi verify-isolation` in the installer. Should return a short human-readable summary and machine parseable JSON for infra automation.
Raj P: For RBAC: require two-person approve for any permanent keystore role change. Enforce via GH PR CODEOWNERS + policy engine.
Sophie L: Security bot suggestion: run a weekly reconciliation job that queries KMS grants and flags any long-lived grants (>4h) for review. :rotating_light:
sec-bot: Automated check: last weekly scan found 3 grants > 6h in staging. File created: /var/reports/kms-long-lived-2025-01-15.log
Alice M: Great. Action items: Carla — add netpol snippet + eBPF checklist to private docs. Bryan — draft installer `verify-isolation` steps. Raj — define `SRE-KMS-Checkout` role with short TTL and required audit tags. Sophie — update audit-forwarder recommendations and SIEM mappings. I'll consolidate into a customer-facing FAQ for private deployments.
Carla S: On it. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Bryan K: I'll start a PR for the installer hook, ping when ready for review.
Raj P: Will write RBAC role proposal and put it in `security/rbac/playbooks`.
Sophie L: I'll update the observability docs and add example Splunk/GCS query.
Alice M: Thanks team — keeping this thread for the docs PRs + follow-ups. If anything urgent, DM. :thumbsup:
